text:
Mikhail Sergachev is doing what Utah traded for: 24:42 a night, 22 points in 25 games, 13 on the power play. He blocks shots too, 42 of them, and the two-time Stanley Cup winner from Tampa is the Mammoth's most important defenseman.

The last week has been quiet. He's pointless in four straight, and in this case the chances have thinned out too, so it isn't just bad luck. Some of the earlier scoring was running hot: six goals on 3.7 expected. The setup work is the sturdier part. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts his primary shot assists at the 94th percentile among defensemen, and the power play runs through him. At five on five Utah takes 55% of the expected goals with him on, though about three points less than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 88th among defensemen last season, modest for his reputation. Our range projects 59 to 82 points, carried mostly by the power play.
